limits-domain.title: Finding real domains
limits-domain.statement: For a fraction, exclude inputs where the denominator is zero. For a real square root, require the radicand to be nonnegative. For a logarithm, require the argument to be positive. Every restriction in the original formula must hold at once.

limits-exclude.title: Simplification and excluded inputs
limits-exclude.statement: Cancel a common factor only where it is nonzero. The original and simplified formulas agree on the original domain. An input excluded before cancellation remains excluded.

limits-angle.title: Radians and the unit circle
limits-angle.statement: A full turn measures $2\pi$ radians or $360^\circ$. To convert $\theta$ radians to degrees, multiply by $\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}$. The point at angle $\theta$ on the unit circle is $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$.

limits-sine-period.title: Sine graphs, amplitude, and period
limits-sine-period.statement: For $y=A\sin x$ with $A\ne0$ and $x$ measured in radians, the amplitude is $\lvert A\rvert$ and the period is $2\pi$.

limits-two-sided.title: One-sided criterion for a limit
limits-two-sided.statement: The finite two-sided limit $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)$ equals $L$ if and only if both one-sided limits exist and $\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)=L$.

limits-sum-difference.title: Sum and difference
limits-sum-difference.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ and $g(x)\to M$ as $x\to a$, with $L$ and $M$ finite, then $\lim_{x\to a}(f(x)\pm g(x))=L\pm M$. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-scalar.title: Scalar multiple
limits-scalar.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$ with $L$ finite and $c$ a real constant, then $\lim_{x\to a}cf(x)=cL$. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-product.title: Product
limits-product.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ and $g(x)\to M$ as $x\to a$, with $L$ and $M$ finite, then $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)g(x)=LM$. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-quotient.title: Quotient
limits-quotient.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ and $g(x)\to M$ as $x\to a$, with $L,M$ finite and $M\ne0$, then $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\frac{L}{M}$. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-power.title: Power
limits-power.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$, with $L$ finite and $n$ a positive integer, then $\lim_{x\to a}(f(x))^n=L^n$. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-root.title: Root
limits-root.statement: If $f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$, with $L$ finite and $n$ a positive integer, then $\lim_{x\to a}\sqrt[n]{f(x)}=\sqrt[n]{L}$. For even $n$, require $L\ge0$ and $f(x)\ge0$ for the nearby inputs. The law also holds for one-sided limits.

limits-subst.title: Substitution for polynomials and rational functions
limits-subst.statement: If $f$ is a polynomial or rational function and $a$ belongs to its domain, then $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a)$.

limits-reciprocal.title: Reciprocal powers near zero
limits-reciprocal.statement: For a positive even integer $n$, $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{1}{(x-a)^n}=+\infty$. For a positive odd integer $n$, $\lim_{x\to a^-}\frac{1}{(x-a)^n}=-\infty$ and $\lim_{x\to a^+}\frac{1}{(x-a)^n}=+\infty$.

limits-squeeze.title: Squeeze Theorem
limits-squeeze.statement: Suppose $\ell(x)\le f(x)\le u(x)$ for all sufficiently nearby $x\ne a$. If $\lim_{x\to a}\ell(x)=\lim_{x\to a}u(x)=L$, then $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L$.

limits-poly-cont.title: Continuity of polynomials and rational functions
limits-poly-cont.statement: Every polynomial and rational function is continuous at every point of its domain. In particular, a rational function is continuous wherever its denominator is nonzero.

limits-ops-cont.title: Operations that preserve continuity
limits-ops-cont.statement: If $f$ and $g$ are continuous on their domains, then $f+g$, $f-g$, $cf$, $fg$, $\frac{f}{g}$, $f^n$, and $\sqrt[n]{f}$ are continuous wherever they are defined, for any real constant $c$ and positive integer $n$. A quotient requires $g(x)\ne0$ and an even root requires $f(x)\ge0$.

limits-comp-cont.title: Continuity and composition
limits-comp-cont.statement: If $g(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$, $F$ is continuous at $L$, and $F(g(x))$ is defined for the nearby inputs under consideration, then $\lim_{x\to a}F(g(x))=F(L)$. In particular, if $g$ is continuous at $a$ and $F$ is continuous at $g(a)$, then $F\circ g$ is continuous at $a$.

limits-trig-cont.title: Continuity of trigonometric functions
limits-trig-cont.statement: The functions $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ are continuous for all real $x$. The function $\tan x$ is continuous wherever $\cos x\ne0$.

limits-trig-zero.title: Sine and cosine limits at zero
limits-trig-zero.statement: For $h$ measured in radians, $\lim_{h\to0}\sin h=0$ and $\lim_{h\to0}\cos h=1$.

limits-ivt.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
limits-ivt.statement: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and $N$ lies between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$, then some $c\in[a,b]$ satisfies $f(c)=N$. If $N$ lies strictly between the endpoint values, then $c\in(a,b)$.

limits-lhospital.title: l’Hospital’s rule
limits-lhospital.statement: Suppose $f$ and $g$ are differentiable near $a$, except possibly at $a$, and $g'(x)\ne0$ there for $x\ne a$. If the quotient has form $0/0$ or $\infty/\infty$ and $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}$ exists, finite or infinite, then $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}$. The same conclusion holds for one-sided limits and limits at $\pm\infty$ with the corresponding hypotheses.

limits-powers-log.title: Indeterminate powers
limits-powers-log.statement: For a positive base $f(x)$ let $y=f(x)^{g(x)}$. Then $\ln y=g(x)\ln f(x)$. If $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)\ln f(x)=L$ is finite, continuity of the exponential gives $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)^{g(x)}=e^L$.

d-tangent.title: Tangent-line equation
d-tangent.statement: If $f'(a)$ exists, the tangent line to the graph of $f$ at $(a,f(a))$ has equation $y-f(a)=f'(a)(x-a)$.

d-continuity.title: Differentiability implies continuity
d-continuity.statement: Let $a$ be in the domain of $f$. If $f'(a)$ exists, then $f$ is continuous at $a$, so $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a)$.

d-motion.title: Speeding up and slowing down
d-motion.statement: For motion on a line with differentiable velocity $v$ and acceleration $a=v'$, the speed $|v|$ increases on intervals where $v$ and $a$ have the same nonzero sign. It decreases where they have opposite signs.

d-newton.title: Newton’s law of motion
d-newton.statement: For an object of constant mass $m$ moving along a line with twice-differentiable position $x(t)$, the net force is $F(t)=m\,\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}$.

d-basic.title: Differentiation rules
d-basic.statement: Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable at $x$, and let $c$ be constant. Then $\frac{d}{dx}c=0$, $\frac{d}{dx}x=1$, $(f\pm g)'=f'\pm g'$, and $(cf)'=cf'$.

d-power.title: Power rule
d-power.statement: For a fixed real exponent $n$ and $x>0$, $\frac{d}{dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}$. For other inputs the formula applies wherever the power is differentiable and the right-hand side is defined. For $n=0$, use the constant rule.

d-product.title: Product rule
d-product.statement: If $f$ and $g$ are differentiable at $x$, then $fg$ is differentiable at $x$ and $(fg)'(x)=f'(x)g(x)+f(x)g'(x)$.

d-quotient.title: Quotient rule
d-quotient.statement: If $f$ and $g$ are differentiable at $x$ and $g(x)\ne0$, then $\frac{f}{g}$ is differentiable at $x$ and $\left(\frac fg\right)'(x)=\frac{g(x)f'(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^2}$.

d-chain.title: Chain rule
d-chain.statement: If $g$ is differentiable at $a$ and $f$ is differentiable at $g(a)$, then $f\circ g$ is differentiable at $a$ and $(f\circ g)'(a)=f'(g(a))\,g'(a)$.

d-compositepower.title: Power rule for a function
d-compositepower.statement: If $g$ is differentiable at $x$ and $u\mapsto u^n$ is differentiable at $g(x)$, then $\frac{d}{dx}[g(x)]^n=n[g(x)]^{n-1}g'(x)$ wherever this expression is defined. For the constant exponent $n=0$, use the constant rule.

d-rates.title: Relating rates with the chain rule
d-rates.statement: Suppose $y(t)=f(x(t))$, $x$ is differentiable at $t_0$, and $f$ is differentiable at $x(t_0)$. Then $\left.\frac{dy}{dt}\right|_{t=t_0}=f'(x(t_0))\left.\frac{dx}{dt}\right|_{t=t_0}$.

d-similar.title: Similar triangles
d-similar.statement: Suppose two triangles with corresponding side lengths $a,b,c$ and $A,B,C$ have equal corresponding angles. Then $\frac{a}{A}=\frac{b}{B}=\frac{c}{C}$. The common ratio is the scaling factor from the triangle with sides $A,B,C$ to the one with sides $a,b,c$.

d-inversetest.title: Inverse functions and the horizontal line test
d-inversetest.statement: A function $f$ has an inverse on its range if and only if $f$ is one-to-one. Equivalently, every horizontal line intersects its graph at most once.

d-inverse.title: Inverse-function derivative
d-inverse.statement: Suppose $f$ is continuous and one-to-one on an open interval containing $a$, differentiable at $a$, and $f'(a)\ne0$. If $b=f(a)$, then $f^{-1}$ is differentiable at $b$ and $(f^{-1})'(b)=\frac{1}{f'(a)}=\frac{1}{f'(f^{-1}(b))}$.

d-invtrig.title: Inverse-trigonometric derivatives
d-invtrig.statement: On the usual inverse-trigonometric branches, measure angles in radians. For $|x|<1$, $(\sin^{-1}x)'=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$ and $(\cos^{-1}x)'=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$. For $x\in\mathbb R$, $(\tan^{-1}x)'=\frac1{1+x^2}$ and $(\cot^{-1}x)'=-\frac1{1+x^2}$. For $|x|>1$, $(\sec^{-1}x)'=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^2-1}}$ and $(\csc^{-1}x)'=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^2-1}}$. Here $\cot^{-1}$ takes values in $(0,\pi)$, $\sec^{-1}$ in $[0,\pi]\setminus\{\pi/2\}$, and $\csc^{-1}$ in $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\setminus\{0\}$.

d-eslope.title: Exponential slope and the existence of e
d-eslope.statement: For $a>0$, the limit $F(a)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{a^h-1}{h}$ exists. The function $F$ is continuous and strictly increasing. There is a unique $e\in(1,10)$ for which $F(e)=1$.

d-base.title: Exponential and logarithmic derivatives in other bases
d-base.statement: If $a>0$, then $\frac{d}{dx}a^x=a^x\ln a$ for all real $x$. If also $a\ne1$ and $x>0$, then $\frac{d}{dx}\log_a x=\frac{1}{x\ln a}$.

d-relative.title: Relative growth
d-relative.statement: If $P(t)=P_0e^{kt}$ with $P_0>0$ and constant $k$, then $P'(t)=kP(t)$ and $\frac{P'(t)}{P(t)}=k$. Positive $k$ gives growth and negative $k$ gives decay.

d-loglaws.title: Exponent and logarithm laws
d-loglaws.statement: Let $a>0$, $r,s\in\mathbb R$, and $M,N>0$. Then $a^{r+s}=a^ra^s$, $a^{r-s}=\frac{a^r}{a^s}$, and $(a^r)^s=a^{rs}$. For $a\ne1$, $\log_a(MN)=\log_a M+\log_a N$, $\log_a(M/N)=\log_a M-\log_a N$, and $\log_a(M^r)=r\log_a M$.

d-variable.title: Logarithmic differentiation of a variable power
d-variable.statement: Suppose $f$ and $g$ are differentiable near $x$ and $f(x)>0$. For $y=f(x)^{g(x)}$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=f(x)^{g(x)}\left(g'(x)\ln f(x)+g(x)\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\right)$.

d-trig.title: Trigonometric derivative formulas
d-trig.statement: Measure angles in radians. For every real $x$, $(\sin x)'=\cos x$ and $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$. Wherever $\cos x\ne0$, $(\tan x)'=\sec^2x$ and $(\sec x)'=\sec x\tan x$. Wherever $\sin x\ne0$, $(\cot x)'=-\csc^2x$ and $(\csc x)'=-\csc x\cot x$.

extreme-value.title: Extreme Value Theorem
extreme-value.statement: If $f$ is continuous on a closed interval $[a,b]$, then $f$ attains a global minimum and a global maximum on $[a,b]$.

fermat.title: Fermat’s theorem
fermat.statement: If $f$ has a local extremum at an interior input $c$, then $c$ is a critical number. In particular, if $f'(c)$ exists, then $f'(c)=0$. An included endpoint must be checked separately.

closed-interval.title: Closed-interval method
closed-interval.statement: For $f$ continuous on $[a,b]$, compare $f(a)$, $f(b)$, and $f(c)$ at every interior critical number $c$. The smallest and largest of these values are the global minimum and maximum.

increasing-decreasing.title: Increasing and decreasing test
increasing-decreasing.statement: Suppose $f$ is differentiable on an open interval $I$. If $f'>0$ throughout $I$, then $f$ is increasing on $I$. If $f'<0$ throughout $I$, then $f$ is decreasing there.

first-derivative.title: First derivative test
first-derivative.statement: Let $c$ be an interior critical number of $f$, with $f$ continuous at $c$. Suppose $f'$ exists and has a strict, constant sign on each side sufficiently near $c$. From left to right, a change from positive to negative gives a strict local maximum, and negative to positive gives a strict local minimum. The same sign on both sides gives neither.

concavity-test.title: Concavity test
concavity-test.statement: If $f''>0$ throughout an interval, the graph of $f$ is concave up there. If $f''<0$ throughout an interval, the graph is concave down there.

second-derivative.title: Second derivative test
second-derivative.statement: Suppose $f'(c)=0$ and $f''$ is continuous on an open interval containing $c$. If $f''(c)>0$, then $f(c)$ is a strict local minimum. If $f''(c)<0$, then $f(c)$ is a strict local maximum. If $f''(c)=0$, the test is inconclusive.

leading-terms.title: End behavior of rational functions
leading-terms.statement: Let $p,q$ be polynomials with leading terms $a_mx^m,b_nx^n$ and $a_mb_n\ne0$. At each of $+\infty$ and $-\infty$, $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ has the same limit as $\frac{a_m}{b_n}x^{m-n}$. Thus $m<n$ gives $0$, $m=n$ gives $\frac{a_m}{b_n}$, and for $m>n$ the sign of the leading-term quotient determines the infinite limit at each end.

polynomial-division.title: Polynomial division
polynomial-division.statement: Given real polynomials $P$ and $Q$ with $Q\ne0$, there are unique polynomials $S$ and $R$ for which $P=QS+R$ and either $R=0$ or $\deg R<\deg Q$.

slant-by-division.title: Slant asymptote by division
slant-by-division.statement: For polynomials $P,Q$ with $Q\ne0$ and $\deg P=\deg Q+1$, the quotient in polynomial division is linear. Its graph is a slant asymptote of $\frac{P}{Q}$ at both infinite ends.

right-triangle.title: Pythagorean theorem
right-triangle.statement: For a right triangle with legs $a,b$ and hypotenuse $c$, $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

trig-identities.title: Unit-circle and angle-addition identities
trig-identities.statement: For any angle $h$, $\sin^2 h+\cos^2 h=1$. The sine addition formula is $\sin(a+h)=\sin a\cos h+\cos a\sin h$.
